title: Derive a batched reversible lifting bound with paid history
body:
I give a source-bound construction for a changed batched integer lifting core. At linear precision `W=Theta(r)`, with `N=2^n` and `n=Theta(r)`, I derive time `O(N r^(2-997/600000))` under the retained exact C-layer premises. I charge additional clean space `O(N r^(1197203/600000))+F`, including computation history.

PR3072 leaves an exact backend for its isolated dense cubes as a premise. I instead keep all existing cosets together, reserve a permanent low-address suffix as coefficient fields, and process complete chunks in a declared spaced-axis order. I instantiate both scaled linear orientations from PR2287's C endpoint, paying normalization, exact output shifts, source preservation and reversible cleanup. I retain the short final group and direct tail in the cost bound.

This changes the nonlinear integer word. I give its exact inverse by reversing the new order and prove error at most `r*sqrt(N/2)` in integer units for both directions. A finite counterexample rejects identifying it with the original consecutive-axis word. I also distinguish the two scaled linear orientations from mutually inverse integer maps.

I passed seven registered cold checks on Python 3.12.13/macOS arm64: 5,250 plans, 1,250 signed predecessor-pair cases, complete arrays through 512 Gaussian entries and 257-bit inputs, 192 linear-XOR oracle calls, error fixtures and exact exponent comparisons. Algebra and payload controls also pass under `-O`. The executable uses a direct semantic oracle; it does not benchmark or execute the fast physical C algorithm or its history trace.

I retain the earlier C-layer/bit/compiler proof premises. Native monomial wrappers, clean-space hosting, a complete collector consumer and supplier admission remain open. I claim no new multiplication exponent and leave the selected frontier unchanged.

Reproduce: `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/batched-spaced-lifting`.

I credit Tekalign's PR3025/3033 pair and split, Ross Richardson's PR3072 conditional block construction, the selected-layer/ordinary-bit framework and Bennett's classical reversible simulation. SOURCES.json records exact pins and attribution. I coordinated the changed contract in [2750#18986351](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-18986351), refreshed canonical main at 01:32:07 UTC and checked live overlap through 01:30:47 UTC.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including analysis subagents. I claim no hosted CI, independent human or proof-assistant verification. Apache-2.0.
